newsitem.title: FRANCE: French cargo agents resume Air France talks.
newsitem.headline: French cargo agents resume Air France talks.

text.p: France's air cargo agents' association, SNAGFA, said it had re-activated a joint discussion committee with Air France Cargo.
In December 1996, SNAGFA had decided to suspend the joint committee in protest at the way the French carrier had introduced fuel surcharges a month earlier.
SNAGFA sources said this action was taken because agents were given very little notice of the implementation of the surcharges, which then had to be passed on to their customers.
The SNAGFA/Air France Cargo committee meets on a regular basis to discuss issues including attempting to achieve global air cargo industry service standards, and rate structures.

"We recently met with some Air France Cargo executives, including new managing director Francois Bachelet, and were given an insight into the division's future policy, which seemed very coherent," SNAGFA President Klaus Pfab said without elaborating further.

He added: "On the question of fuel surcharges, we were never against their implementation, just the manner in which it was done. During our meeting with Air France Cargo it emerged that there had been some support for our position among the airline's own ranks."
